title: A Practical Strategy for Exploring the Pharmacological Mechanism of Luteolin Against COVID-19/Asthma Comorbidity: Findings of System Pharmacology and Bioinformatics Analysis.
authors: Xie, Yi-Zi; Peng, Chen-Wen; Su, Zu-Qing; Huang, Hui-Ting; Liu, Xiao-Hong; Zhan, Shao-Feng; Huang, Xiu-Fang
one_liner_zh: 该文研究木犀草素对COVID-19/哮喘合并症的药理机制，仅涉及药物-蛋白对接，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Asthma patients may increase their susceptibility to SARS-CoV-2 infection and the poor prognosis of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). However, anti-COVID-19/asthma comorbidity approaches are restricted on condition. Existing evidence indicates that luteolin has antiviral, anti-inflammatory, and immune regulation capabilities. We aimed to evaluate the possibility of luteolin evolving into an ideal drug and explore the underlying molecular mechanisms of luteolin against COVID-19/asthma comorbidity. We used system pharmacology and bioinformatics analysis to assess the physicochemical properties and biological activities of luteolin and further analyze the binding activities, targets, biological functions, and mechanisms of luteolin against COVID-19/asthma comorbidity. We found that luteolin may exert ideal physicochemical properties and bioactivity, and molecular docking analysis confirmed that luteolin performed effective binding activities in COVID-19/asthma comorbidity. Furthermore, a protein-protein interaction network of 538 common targets between drug and disease was constructed and 264 hub targets were obtained. Then, the top 6 hub targets of luteolin against COVID-19/asthma comorbidity were identified, namely, TP53, AKT1, ALB, IL-6, TNF, and VEGFA. Furthermore, the enrichment analysis suggested that luteolin may exert effects on virus defense, regulation of inflammation, cell growth and cell replication, and immune responses, reducing oxidative stress and regulating blood circulation through the Toll-like receptor; MAPK, TNF, AGE/RAGE, EGFR, ErbB, HIF-1, and PI3K-AKT signaling pathways; PD-L1 expression; and PD-1 checkpoint pathway in cancer. The possible "dangerous liaison" between COVID-19 and asthma is still a potential threat to world health. This research is the first to explore whether luteolin could evolve into a drug candidate for COVID-19/asthma comorbidity. This study indicated that luteolin with superior drug likeness and bioactivity has great potential to be used for treating COVID-19/asthma comorbidity, but the predicted results still need to be rigorously verified by experiments.
abstract_zh: 哮喘患者可能增加对SARS-CoV-2感染的易感性及2019冠状病毒病（COVID-19）的不良预后。然而，针对COVID-19/哮喘共病的治疗策略受到条件限制。现有证据表明，木犀草素具有抗病毒、抗炎及免疫调节能力。我们旨在评估木犀草素发展为理想药物的可能性，并探讨其对抗COVID-19/哮喘共病的潜在分子机制。我们采用系统药理学和生物信息学分析，评估木犀草素的理化性质及生物活性，并进一步分析木犀草素对抗COVID-19/哮喘共病的结合活性、靶点、生物学功能及机制。我们发现，木犀草素可能具有理想的理化性质和生物活性，分子对接分析证实木犀草素在COVID-19/哮喘共病中表现出有效的结合活性。此外，构建了药物与疾病之间538个共同靶点的蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络，并获得了264个核心靶点。随后，确定了木犀草素对抗COVID-19/哮喘共病的排名前6的核心靶点，即TP53、AKT1、ALB、IL-6、TNF和VEGFA。进一步富集分析表明，木犀草素可能通过Toll样受体、MAPK、TNF、AGE/RAGE、EGFR、ErbB、HIF-1和PI3K-AKT信号通路，以及PD-L1表达和癌症中的PD-1检查点通路，发挥抗病毒、调节炎症、细胞生长和细胞复制、免疫反应、减少氧化应激及调节血液循环的作用。COVID-19与哮喘之间可能的“危险联系”仍是对世界健康的潜在威胁。本研究首次探讨木犀草素是否能成为COVID-19/哮喘共病的候选药物。研究表明，具有优良药物相似性和生物活性的木犀草素在治疗COVID-19/哮喘共病方面具有巨大潜力，但预测结果仍需通过实验严格验证。
